findings.title: TTL cleanup deletes a deduplicated file still retained by a sent attachment
normalTrigger: Same cwd/session and same valid image bytes staged twice; second stage reuses absPath but receives a different ID.
One staged ID remains draft; the other is marked sent normally.
No-sessionId TTL cleanup runs when draft is at least24h old and sent entry is still within30d.
findings.cause: Cleanup reduces state by attachmentID and unlinks each expired ID path without checking other retained IDs sharing the same content file.
findings.effect: Canonical backing file for a still-retained sent attachment is unlinked; recent projection omits its metadata when the file is missing. No actual user data deletion or UI frame was observed by this author.
counterEvidenceAndLimits: Different-session hash reuse has separate storage paths and is not affected by this shared-path cause.
cleanup with explicitsessionId intentionally removes the whole session and is not this defect.
The existing TTL test uses different sessions; ordinary hash-reuse test separately requires identicalpath/differentID.
Marking all shared IDs sent can avoid the early draft branch; both references expiring normally is not this defect.
No malformed image, hash collision, restart ID collision, Date mocking or artificial failed I/O is needed.
findings.suggestedRepair: Retire expired metadata perID, but unlink a canonicalpath only when every live reference to that path is expired or removed.
